newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-BELGIAN CHAMPIONS LIERSE SKINNED ALIVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BELGIAN CHAMPIONS LIERSE SKINNED ALIVE.

text.p: Most clubs want to avoid Belgium's league champions in the European Cup draw.
Next time they may be lining up for the honour.

New champions Lierse have already been stripped of half the team through end-of-season transfers with other key players likely to follow. Their coach, hailed as the architect of their unexpected triumph, is gone too.

Lierse's dazzling play earned them their first title since 1960, won the hearts of Belgian soccer fans across the linguistic frontier dividing the country into French and Dutch-speaking communities, and sparked a mega-party in the streets of hometown Lier.
It also sparked a stampede of club managers armed with lucrative contracts which Lierse, with its average crowd of 8,500, could not match.
"This is the downside of the medal. People come to watch a successful team that brings attractive soccer," said departing coach Eric Gerets.
"Our chairman is heart-broken about what is happening now."

Four Lierse players -- defenders Eric Van Meir and Bart De Roover, midfielder Nico Van Kerckhoven and striker Bob Peeters -- have all become regular Belgian internationals this season, which further raised their appeal for other clubs.
Peeters has signed with Roda and De Roover is said to be in talks with another Dutch club, NAC Breda.
PSV Eindhoven has said its interested in Van Meir and Van Kerckhoven might be tempted to go to UEFA Cup winners Schalke 04 of Germany.
Lierse's former Dutch international goalkeeper Stanley Menzo is definitely moving to Bordeaux, Brazilian striker Zefilho and midfielder Dirk Huysmans go to Standard Liege.
Denis Kliouev is set to move to Schalke 04 and midfielder Karel Snoeckx is on his way to ambitious Belgian club Lokeren.
Gerets is moving to last year's champions Club Brugge and will be succeeded at Lierse by Standard Liege coach Jos Daerden.
Still Lierse chairman Freddy Van Laer insists nobody else will be jumping ship.

"Nobody else will be allowed to leave," he said amid reports that Ajax were pulling the shirt sleeves of former Poland and FC Cologne midfielder Andrzej Rudy, who arrived at Lierse only last September and is now dubbed "the general".
"It is deeply sad that the new champion has been plucked like an ordinary chicken," Het Nieuwsblad newspaper said.
"Gerets, Huysmans, Snoeckx, Kliouev, Zefilho, Peeters and Menzo are leaving the party boat and the vultures are still circling above (players) like Van Kerckhoven, De Roover and Van Meir," it said.
Observers and opponents agreed Lierse, who lost just three times, had been outstanding.
"They deserved to be the champions," said Belgium and Club Brugge midfielder Franky Van der Elst. Brugge finished runners-up, two points behind.
The Lierse players too said it had been a wonderful year and some insisted it had been the best time of their life. But they also insisted they have to make a living.
